method: Original summaries checked against named publisher, author or catalogue sources. Edition identity and content evidence are distinguished; no source excerpt is copied into the summaries.

entries.title: Summa Theologiae
entries.author: Thomas Aquinas
entries.sourceName: Cambridge University Press via Google Books
entries.text: This edition contains the third volume of Thomas Aquinas's Summa Theologiae, Knowing and Naming God, covering questions 12 and 13 of the first part. Its subject is how human beings can know God and what theological language can express about the divine. The volume places Latin alongside English and belongs to the English Dominicans' edition, bringing these philosophical and theological questions together in a self-contained part of the larger work.

evidence.basis: Google Books identifies Thomas Aquinas, editor Herbert McCabe, Cambridge University Press, 1990, exact ISBN 9780521393508, volume 3, title Knowing and Naming God and questions 1a. 12-13. Its publisher description identifies the Latin/English Dominican edition. Search retrieval succeeded; a later direct open returned cache miss.

Exact ISBN, author and editor corroborated. Publisher contents cover knowing God and theological language; description states parallel Latin and English and that each volume is self-contained. No claims about the entire Summa being contained in this ISBN.

entries.identityNotes: Live edition title is abbreviated to Summa Theologiae. Exact ISBN represents volume 3, not the entire work; summary makes that scope explicit. Do not use on other Summa ISBNs.

entries.title: Tweede persoon enkelvoud
entries.author: Sayed Qashu
entries.text: Een advocaat in Oost-Jeruzalem vindt in een tweedehands boek een persoonlijk briefje dat zijn vrouw lijkt te hebben geschreven. Zijn achterdocht zet hem op een zoektocht naar de ontvanger. Daarnaast volgt de roman een Palestijns-Israëlische maatschappelijk werker die zorgt voor een jonge Joodse man in coma. De twee verhalen raken met elkaar verweven en verbinden vragen over trouw en verlangen met identiteit en de behoefte ergens bij te horen.

evidence.basis: Apple Books labels the text Publisher Description and identifies AmboAnthos, Sayed Kashua and Dutch. Confirms the lawyer's discovery, the caregiver's parallel story, the comatose patient and identity themes. This is the ebook listing; used for work content, not to claim paperback format or pagination.

Exact Dutch paperback ISBN 9789041418371, title Tweede persoon enkelvoud, author Sayed Kashua, publisher Anthos and translator Ruben Verhasselt. Supports identity of the selected edition; no ratings or reviews used.
Independently confirms title, Sayed Kashua, Ambo/Anthos and exact ISBN 9789041418371; supplied description agrees on both plot strands.

entries.identityNotes: Live author string is Sayed Qashu, whereas Dutch publisher/catalog display Sayed Kashua. Keep exact current author as guard; the exact ISBN and Dutch title identify the same edition. Do not silently broaden author matching.

entries.title: Eyes of the Tailless Animals
entries.author: Soon Ok Lee
entries.sourceName: Soon Ok Lee — U.S. Senate testimony
entries.text: Soon Ok Lee recounts her imprisonment in North Korea after a career in government administration. Her memoir describes interrogation, forced labour and the treatment of fellow prisoners, drawing on what she says she witnessed while working in a prison's accounting office. The account follows her experience of losing the protection of the state she had trusted and her efforts to make prisoners' experiences known after leaving North Korea.

evidence.basis: Author testimony states prior government supply-office work, arrest, interrogation, prison factory and accounting assignments, and publication of her Korean memoir to tell others about prisoners' experiences. Specific allegations remain attributed to her account; no universal reliability or sole-survivor claim is made.

NII/CiNii catalog identifies Eyes of the tailless animals: prison memoirs of a North Korean woman, Soon Ok Lee, English translation, Living Sacrifice Book Co. 1999, ISBN10 0882643355. ISBN13 equivalent is 9780882643359.
USCIRF identifies the witness Soon-Ok Lee as author of Eyes of the Tailless Animals, linking author testimony to the English book title.
Record matches exact ISBN13, title and author. No community-written synopsis or review was used, and the summary does not depend on Open Library wording.

entries.identityNotes: Soon Ok Lee, Soon-Ok Lee and Yi Sun-ok are represented in catalog authority forms. Exact current title/author/ISBN remain the implementation guard. Dates and imprisonment durations are deliberately omitted because source accounts vary.

entries.title: The Mediterranean Caper
entries.author: Clive Cussler
entries.text: An attack on a U.S. air base on a Greek island brings Dirk Pitt into a mystery involving an aircraft from the First World War. Working with Al Giordino and NUMA, he investigates the connection between the assault and sabotage aimed at a scientific expedition. The search draws him into a smuggling operation, where identifying the people behind the attacks becomes a struggle to stay alive.

evidence.basis: Publisher description confirms Greek island, attack on U.S. air base by a First World War aircraft, Dirk Pitt, Al Giordino, NUMA, sabotage of scientific expedition and international smuggling. Publisher page is for later ISBN 9780425197394; used for shared novel content, not the selected edition's format or date.
Catalog edition OL24945125M identifies title The Mediterranean Caper, Clive Cussler, ISBN10 0671670425, ISBN13 9780671670429 and English edition. Used only for identity, not description wording.
Confirms exact ISBN 9780671670429, Clive Cussler, English and Pocket Books.

entries.identityNotes: Summary covers plot shared by the selected Pocket Books edition and the publisher's later edition; it makes no edition-specific pagination or series numbering claim.

entries.title: Undaunted Courage
entries.author: Stephen E. Ambrose
entries.text: Stephen E. Ambrose follows Meriwether Lewis from his relationship with Thomas Jefferson to the expedition he led with William Clark across the American West. The narrative traces the journey toward the Pacific while examining its scientific aims, political ambitions and physical dangers. Encounters with Native American communities, the work of Sacagawea and the partnership between the two captains place Lewis's personal story within the larger history of the expedition.

evidence.basis: Publisher identifies Stephen E. Ambrose, title Undaunted Courage, subtitle, and ISBN13 9780684826974. About the Book covers Jefferson's selection of Lewis, the route to the Pacific, scientific aims, terrain and weather, Clark, Sacagawea and Native American leaders. No marketing superlatives or unsupported discovery claims are retained.

entries.identityNotes: Exact selected title, author and ISBN all match the publisher page.

entries.title: The Universe Versus Alex Woods
entries.author: Gavin Extence
entries.sourceName: Hachette Book Group / Redhook via NetGalley
entries.text: A childhood encounter with a meteorite leaves Alex Woods marked out from other children. Bullied at school and raised by a fortune teller, he forms an unexpected friendship with the older, widowed Mr. Peterson. Their relationship leads him to consider how to live on his own terms. At seventeen, being stopped at customs brings the unusual choices he has made into public view.

evidence.basis: NetGalley publisher entry identifies Hachette Book Group / Redhook, Gavin Extence, exact title and ISBN 9780316246576. Description supports meteorite injury in childhood, fortune-teller mother, bullying, friendship with widower Mr. Peterson, and customs stop at seventeen. New summary removes OCR errors and promotional praise from the currently rendered Open Library source.

entries.identityNotes: Saved public HTML serializes storedDescription as $undefined and resolves a dynamic open_library description. An exact-edition reviewed fallback can replace that provider text without altering the precedence of centrally stored reviewed content.

entries.title: Where Do Chicks Come From? (Let's-Read-and-Find-Out Science 1)
entries.author: Amy E. Sklansky
entries.text: A hen sitting on her eggs is the starting point for this illustrated introduction to how a chick develops. Amy E. Sklansky follows the changes inside a fertilized egg and explains the mother's role in keeping it warm until hatching. With pictures by Pam Paparone, the book introduces young readers to a stage of a chicken's life that is usually hidden inside the shell.

evidence.basis: Author's own book page confirms subject, illustrator, publisher and development from fertilized egg to hatching.
Catalog confirms exact ISBN, author, illustrator and series. Parenthetical series in LumiScore's edition title refers to the same ISBN.

entries.title: Hard Eight (Stephanie Plum Series #8)
entries.author: Janet Evanovich
entries.text: A request from a neighbour draws Stephanie Plum into the search for a missing child. What begins as a favour becomes dangerous when the disappearance leads toward Eddie Abruzzi and threats against Stephanie herself. With her relationship with Joe Morelli unsettled, she turns to Ranger for help. This eighth Stephanie Plum novel combines the investigation with the complications of Stephanie's family, colleagues and love life.

evidence.basis: Publisher confirms exact ISBN, author, eighth Stephanie Plum novel, missing child, Morelli and Ranger.
Author confirms neighbour's request, Eddie Abruzzi's involvement and threats.

entries.title: Grief Is the Thing with Feathers
entries.author: Max Porter
entries.text: After their mother's sudden death, two boys and their father struggle to inhabit a changed home in London. Their grief attracts an unexpected visitor: Crow, whose disruptive presence offers both trouble and comfort. He intends to remain until the family can manage without him. Max Porter brings the voices of the father, children and bird together in a short work about loss, memory and the gradual reshaping of family life.

evidence.basis: Exact Faber ISBN, author and publisher description confirm London family, sudden loss, Crow and eventual healing. Original paraphrase, no review blurbs used.

entries.title: The Tale of the Body Thief
entries.author: Anne Rice
entries.text: Lestat accepts Raglan James's offer to exchange bodies, hoping to experience mortal life again. The experiment becomes a trap when James disappears with the vampire's body and its powers. Confined to an unfamiliar human existence, Lestat must find a way to reverse the exchange. The fourth Vampire Chronicles novel turns questions about identity, desire and the separation of body and soul into a pursuit of what Lestat has lost.

evidence.basis: Author's official catalogue describes temporary body exchange, James's disappearance, recovery attempt and body/soul theme; confirms fourth series volume.
Exact 9780345384751 identifies the English Random House edition of this work.

entries.title: There's a Boy in the Girls' Bathroom
entries.author: Louis Sachar
entries.text: Bradley Chalkers is older than the other children in his fifth-grade class and has a reputation for lying and starting fights. Expecting rejection, he finds it difficult to imagine anyone seeing him differently. Carla, the new school counsellor, notices qualities that others overlook and encourages him to try changing. Louis Sachar's story follows a boy learning to question the hostile picture of himself that has taken hold at school.

evidence.basis: Publisher's work description confirms Bradley, fifth grade, behavioural problems, Carla and fear of trying to change.
Bibliographic identity only: exact 9780679805960 and Louis Sachar. Summary is independently paraphrased from publisher, not withdrawn Open Library text.
